_: The facts dialogue states: one row per fact (id, says, cues). A pool line names the facts it states in factIds; an override names the ones it carries. A cue is a word or phrase that shows a line states the fact (whole word, case-blind; a cue ending in an asterisk matches any ending). Hearing a line teaches its facts.

entries.says: A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own.
All the Hist share one mind through their roots.
Argonians hatch beside a Hist.
Argonians drink the sap of the Hist.
On the naming day each hatchling drinks the Hist's sap.
The sap shapes the child's body and scales for life.
The sap becomes an Argonian's blood and soul. At death the spirit goes back to its Hist.
The eggs lie in a clutch near the roots of the Hist.
The tree-minder reads the Hist's signs and tells the tribe how the clutch fares.
Helstrom is the capital of the Argonian interior.
Helstrom is a city grown into a Hist grove.
The native armies withdrew to Helstrom after the Battle of Argonia.
The Empire chose not to besiege Helstrom. No army has ever taken it.
Ojel is the Argonian word for outsiders.
Ojel is a plain word and carries no insult.
Lukiul is a slur that the An-Xileel coined for assimilated Argonians.
Argonians hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist.
The Many-Root Conclave is an order of Hist stewards.
The Conclave's minders keep the trees.
The Conclave sees that each tree is asked for its consent.
The Conclave sends minders out to the villages.
A tree-minder tends one Hist and reads its signs and its will.
A minder feels when the eggs or the tribe are in trouble.
The An-Xileel are the nativist government of Argonia.
The An-Xileel began as a party in the Oblivion Crisis.
The An-Xileel drove the Empire out of Black Marsh.
The An-Xileel want the province free of Imperial ways.
The Veiled Reed is the covert office of the An-Xileel.
The Veiled Reed's agents guard the province against its enemies by secrecy and coercion.
The Veiled Reed's factors travel the interior as its agents.
Tappers draw sap from the trees.
Cult couriers and tappers stay at the Greenspring lodge on the way to Helstrom.
Salt is reaching the Greenspring spring.
The salt comes from the salt works upstream, which the village blames.
The lodge talk is of who will carry the next load to Helstrom.
A silent Hist has stopped speaking to its tribe.
A Hist can fall silent when it is sick or shuts itself off from the other Hist.
Cutters are working at the edge of a Hist grove inland.
The lodge is the village inn for travellers bound for Helstrom.
A bed costs one price a night that the village agreed together.
The lodge sells rope.
Water from the spring is free to any traveller.
The spring families cook at the fire stands.
The spring families fill the lodge jars.
The spring families mend rope to sell.
When two families quarrel, the tree-minder hears both sides and settles it.
A root-herald bargains over trade.
A root-herald is a tribe's envoy to the outside world.
A root-herald gathers news.
The root-herald's office is the tribe's own and holds no rank in the state.
Greenspring's herald keeps a ledger of goods sent down the road to Helstrom.
Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet.
Travellers bound for Helstrom stop at Greenspring for water and a bed.
The spring water can be drunk unboiled, which is rare in the region.
The spring is a clear pool under the Hist, ringed by boulders.
The spring-keeper holds the ladle on its cord at the stone lip.
Visitors are expected to taste the water before they speak.
The tree-minder tends the village Hist.
The tree-minder clears the fallen leaves from the root each dusk.
A net-mender makes torn nets and worn gear sound again.
The net-mender works in the open, where anyone can watch.
Anyone may bring a net to be mended.
The flotilla speaker speaks for the lighter crews when the council writes.
The speaker calls the crews to a vote on the council's letter.
No hull casts off without the speaker's nod.
The crews once stopped the port for two weeks over a licence.
Every cargo in the bay comes ashore in a lighter's hold.
The lighter's master casts off the Lilmoth lighter.
The Lilmoth lighter carries passengers between the city pier and the anchorage.
A lighter meets deep-water ships and takes their cargo.
The purser keeps the trade ship's books.
The purser sells the ship's goods untaxed.
The purser lets bunks below deck for a fare.
Bog iron forms in stagnant water rich in iron.
A digger lifts bog iron from the seep in cakes.
The furnace is built new each season and broken open for the bloom.
Each digger goes home to a different village at season's end.
A lot is a numbered stretch of seabed.
Each lot passes down one diver family and no other may dive it.
A lot diver fills a net with shells and grades them by size before any is opened.
The tally book records the takings and the drownings alike.
The surface tender minds the boat and the divers' lines from above.
The tender never enters the water.
The diver families share the tenders.
The tenders are moored over the lots.
The tag-keeper hangs a tag on every basket.
Every carriage charge is written in the book before the bundle is wrapped.
A body leaves the Rose's hands only under the shelter, never on the road.
A body is never handed over without its tag.
The carrier wraps each body from the Rose and carries it home to the villages.
The Rose releases the dead.
The Chainbreakers pay the carriage charge.
Bones brought to the dirt near a tree can still go home.
The Rose is the old prison south of Blackrose.
Families born in the Rose three generations deep live in it now.
The families will not call the Rose a prison.
The carriage charge is the most resented coin in the south.
A dyer buys cut reed by the armful.
The dyer steeps the reed in the vat.
The dye stains the dyer's hands to the wrist.
The dyer buys reed from the cutters along the bank.
Reed is cut along the bank.
The cut reed is tied in bundles.
Reed is sold by the armful.
The buyers of reed are the dyer and whoever is building.
A smith works iron at the forge.
A smith mends the household tools of a settlement.
Bog iron smelted into a bloom is the raw metal a forge works.
A smith is paid in coin or in kind.
Some households have every adult downriver on the roll.
The households who stayed keep the trade-house and the smokehouse.
They keep a kin-house swept for whoever comes back.
More adults go downriver every year and fewer return.
The elder keeps the guest stores by the door.
The elder houses strangers under the elder's roof.
Quarrels and debts between households are brought to the elder.
The elder sees that the offerings at the tree's foot stay filled.
The column was a body of Legion soldiers on the border road.
The Legion was recalled about two centuries ago.
The column's men had not been paid.
Part of the column did not march home.
The Legion never paid those men.
The talk at the Mile House is that Gideon may offer the men of the column a pardon and a wage.
The watch is called on the hour, day and night.
The serjeant keeps the duty roster in his own hand.
The pay book still holds the column's last entry.
The serjeant parleys with a stranger before he fights.
The band works in turns.
One of the band stands at the gate totems.
One watches the bend and whistles when a walker comes into view.
One smokes hides at the fire while the rest sleep.
The lieutenant gives the camp's orders.
Every load taken gets a notched tally stick as its receipt.
The load is taken and the walker goes free.
A dead walker brings his tribe against the camp.
A robbed walker comes back next season.
A boat crew poles and loads its boat along the channel.
A boat crew sleeps at whatever landing the boat reaches by dark.
Riverwalk grows no food of its own.
Riverwalk feeds boat crews and gives each a bunk.
A long house holds a household and its guests under one roof.
The Riverwalk long house stands on piles in the shallows.
The family has kept the Riverwalk long house a long time.
Reed mattresses in the long house are aired every dry morning.
Boats moor at the stage.
Passengers pay their fares on the stage before boarding.
The stage calls each crew by the name of its boat.
A passenger is called traveller until fed.
The toll is a levy on each boat, written down and paid at the toll post.
The toll is charged on boats entering the pilgrim water.
Each boat is written on a slate with one column for Thorn and one for Hissmir.
Thorn and Hissmir each claim the toll.
A priest of the Teeth rings the bell that pilgrims hear from the landing.
The priests hold the bell and the teaching.
The band below the priests holds the stair.
The nisswo meets each pilgrim and asks for the offering.
The band at the Teeth keeps the watch on the stair.
The band carries in the offerings.
The band stands in the shallows through each rite.
Watching, carrying and scrubbing are the temple's whole daily rite.
The nisswo asks each pilgrim what offering they bring.
Nisswo are Argonian priests of Sithis.
Outsiders enter the Teeth only with the right offering.
The scrubber carries a bucket up from the landing.
The stone is scrubbed down to the waterline.
The scrubbing is a ritual. Nothing is repaired or added.
The band leaves untouched the stone beneath the waterline.
A walker can wade the ford, but a cart cannot.
The poler takes carts over on a plank raft.
The poler charges by the wheel.
Taking a cart across without paying the poler is forbidden.
Claywater is two halves at one ford.
Each bank charges a traveller for its own half of the stop.
The station half is built of timber and stone.
The landing half is built of mud and thatch.
The station well is cracking.
The landing is older than the station, and polers worked the ford before the well was dug.
The landing half will not help to repair the well in stone.
The landing's people gave up building in stone long ago and build in mud and timber.
Neither half can hold the other's half of the stop.
The road is the Blackwood Road, an Imperial road.
The road carries carts between Leyawiin and Gideon.
The Mile House of the Eagle and Cartwright's Cross lie along the road.
The road closes in the monsoon season.
The station well is Imperial-built stone.
The well is drawn by a windlass at set hours.
A traveller asks the well-keeper before drawing water.
Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast south of the stage.
The families hold hereditary salvage rights.
Each family guards its own stretch of shore.
Taking timber from another family's stretch is forbidden.
The stall sells the past week's salvage.
Each lot is counted at the stall before it is sold.
A lot is sold under its ship's name, read off the bow-board.
A lot without its ship's name is not sold.
Chasepoint is an Imperial road stage.
The stage-keeper's office is inherited.
No keeper has been paid since the coast road stopped being kept.
Two families each claim the keeper's office.
A gang is hands who owe money to House Dres.
A gang hand dredges the channel off the barge.
A gang hand sleeps on land with the family.
Food, sickness and broken tools are added to the debt.
A clutch is a family's eggs.
The clutch-keeper keeps the hatching shed's fire low.
The clutch-keeper keeps the nest dry.
Dry reed for the nest comes from the basket by the door.
The roll is the list of hands who owe the house.
The roll is read on the barge, never in the camp.
A witness knows every family and every name on the roll.
The witness can say who saw a thing done in the camp.
Two overseers keep the gang's debts.
House Dres is the old slaving house.
One overseer sits by the fire with the ledger.
The other overseer checks each door at dusk.
Large ships cannot dock at Lilmoth.
A lighter hand hauls cargo from the anchorage into the lighter's hold.
A lighter hand bails between runs.
A lighter hand sleeps in a bunk below the foredeck.
Thorn is the northern border city of the saltrice fields.
The Tear road runs from Thorn into Morrowind.
House Dres once raided Thorn for slaves and profited from its rice.
The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord argues over who holds title to the saltrice fields.
Hissmir is a pilgrimage xanmeer in southern Shadowfen.
Outsiders and Argonians with no Hist can commune with the Hist at Hissmir.
A comer at Hissmir must pass its trials first.
The Root Stewards run the trials at Hissmir and cannot refuse anyone who comes.
Shells and Stones is played on a marked reed mat.
Boat crews play Shells and Stones through the evenings in their crews' house.
Players stake things on Shells and Stones, even the best bunk.
Sithis is the void god of change.
Argonian priests teach that a death is a change.
A death is to be mourned and then released.
The Nisswo are the priests of Sithis.
The Nisswo travel so that each village hears many readings of the faith.
The Nisswo keep no single doctrine and no central rule.
Gideon is the western frontier city.
Gideon is the first settlement on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil.
Gideon's courts still work.
An Owing made in Gideon is a paper contract that can be contested in court.
The Panther Race is the river that comes down from Cyrodiil.
The Panther Race forks by Greenspring and Helstrom.
The Panther Race frogs have a chirp that musicians prize.
The Pantherfish is a prized catch of the Panther Race.
The Legion built the Chasepoint road stage.
Wreck-salvage families keep Chasepoint.
Salvage rights at Chasepoint are hereditary.
Two families each claim the keeper's office at Chasepoint.
Lilmoth is built over shallow water, so large ships anchor out.
A council of merchants rules Lilmoth.
Lilmoth was destroyed in 4E 48 and rebuilt smaller.
The flying city Umbriel destroyed Lilmoth.
The Reed-Sail Compact is the guild of boat crews, routes and ferries.
The Compact runs the boats on the rivers and the coast.
The Salt-Teeth are pirates who sail inside the Compact.
The Compact fixes each crew's share of a route.
The Compact holds its monopoly by stoppage.
A council that tried to license the cargo boats at Lilmoth met a two-week stoppage.
The Counted Lots are numbered pearl beds.
Diver families hold each lot by inheritance.
The deep lots pay best and kill divers.
The tally book records the pay and the deaths.
Archon is the eastern port and the province's legal harbour.
Archon has marsh to the north and beaches to the south.
Pilot families bring ships into Archon through the estuary approach.
The harbour authority's power stops at the headland.
Portdun Mont is a pilots' village.
Pilot families are paid to bring ships through the approach.
The pilots' monopoly is custom with no law behind it.
Portdun Mont stands above a beach landing near the pearl lots.
The Chainbreakers are abolitionists who fight the Owing.
The Chainbreakers audit the Owing.
The Chainbreakers burn the debts they can prove false.
The Chainbreakers carry the bones of the dead home.
The Chainbreakers hold that freeing debtors and carrying the dead home are one work.
A debtor who dies far from the Hist may never get home.
Blackrose is a lake city in the south.
Three rivers meet at Blackrose.
The Rose is Blackrose's old Imperial prison, a day's march south of the city.
Families live in the Rose now.
The Chainbreakers built the Tag House to receive the bones of those who die in the Rose.
The Rose's families release the dead for a carriage charge.
The Chainbreakers pay the carriage charge and record every payment.
The Legion remnant is the garrisons that stayed when the Empire withdrew.
The heirs of the garrisons count as Legion too.
The Legion built the old road stages.
The Prison road, the Border road and the Mile House are old Imperial roads and a waystation.
People still call the old Imperial roads by their old names.
The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on a dry rise.
The Owing is debt that binds a person to labour until it is paid.
The Owing is the marsh's law where there is no court.
An Owing can be sold and passed down.
A person can be born owing.
Naga are a tall adder-like breed of Argonian.
Tribeless Naga belong to no tribe.
Many tribeless Naga rob the tracks while merchants walk them.
Cut-Rope's raiders are one band of tribeless Naga.
More adults go downriver on the roll each year.
The roll is the list of debtors in the dredging gang.
The roll is read out on the barge and never in the camp.
The Cut Circle is a long stilt hall over still water at a lagoon's edge.
The Cut Circle lies within a day of Helstrom.
One walk on piles leads in to the Cut Circle from the land.
The Unbound Root preaches at the Cut Circle in the open.
Alten Corimont is a river port in eastern Shadowfen.
Argonian pirates and smugglers run Alten Corimont.
Alten Corimont takes no side in a war and takes any crew.
The dredging gangs of the lower channel are hired out of Alten Corimont.
Alten Meerhleel is a trade port and floating village north-west of Lilmoth.
A harbormaster built Alten Meerhleel so the tribes could trade with outsiders.
The harbormaster built a court north of the docks to quiet the tribes' complaint.
The Archeins are Argonian families who served the slavers.
The Archeins ran serf villages for the Empire.
Other Argonians hate the Archeins for selling their own people.
Black Marsh took the name Argonia when it left the Empire.
Argonia is a marsh country.
Argonia is ruled from inside the marsh, not by an emperor.
The Argonians are the lizard-folk native to Black Marsh.
Saxhleel is the Argonians' own word for themselves.
The sap of its Hist makes each tribe look a little different.
Argonians have a natural gift for magic and for stealth.
The Battle of Argonia broke the last organised Argonian army.
The survivors of the battle settled at Helstrom.
The Emperor would not send soldiers into the interior after the survivors.
The Blackguards are Argonian pirates and brigands of the south coast.
The Blackguards descend from the inmates of Blackrose Prison.
The Blackguards are the largest band of criminals in Murkmire.
Blackwood is the hilly country in the west of Black Marsh.
The Blackwood Road climbs through Blackwood to Cyrodiil.
The people of the Blackwood hills like riddles.
Bog iron forms where seeping water leaves a crust of iron in the ground.
The Bog Iron Workings lies below the road.
The crews smelt the iron cakes in a clay furnace.
Bones-And-Tools is a hollow under the root layer deep in the jungle.
A creature has made its lair in Bones-And-Tools.
Families driven from the foraging live at the hiring camp a kilometre east.
Bretic means of the Bretons.
The Bretons are a human people of the west.
An Argonian calls a Breton traveller an ojel.
The Bright-Throats breed horse-lizards.
The Bright-Throats welcome outsiders.
The Bright-Throats seal an alliance with a bonding ceremony.
The Broke Column is what is left of a Legion column.
The Legion never paid the men of the Broke Column when it was recalled.
The Broke Column camp stands on a bench above the Mile House track.
The College of Whispers is a society of discreet mages.
The College summons Daedra and raises the dead.
The College has studied Umbriel more closely than any other body.
The Cyrodilic Collections digs up Argonian relics.
The Collections offers to return the relics to Black Marsh.
The Collections has not built its museum of Argonian history.
The Dunmer are the dark elves of Morrowind.
House Dres ran the Argonian slave trade for centuries.
Morrowind ended slavery long ago, but the grievance remains.
A clutch is a family's eggs, laid near the roots of the Hist.
The egg-tender looks after the clutch until the eggs hatch.
The egg-tender writes down each egg's parents, hatch day and star sign.
The eggs of a clutch depend on the Hist beside them.
Fish-Eye Rye is a liquor from Hissmir.
A drinker of Fish-Eye Rye plugs the nostrils.
Gang Ground is the camp of a dredging gang's families.
Gang Ground stands on firm ground between the Border road and the marsh.
The gang's clutch lies in a hatching shed on the top terrace.
The sap of a Hist is the tree's soul.
The Argonians drink the sap at hatching and again at coming of age.
Too much sap poisons an Argonian with a gold mouth and bark-thick scales.
The sap is a drug that stirs bloodlust in an outsider.
The House Dres remnant are the house's surviving claimants.
House Dres built its wealth on Argonian slaves.
The remnant pursue the house's northern interests.
The Empire held the coasts and borders of Black Marsh but not the deep marsh.
The Empire built roads, road stages and prisons.
The Empire withdrew from Black Marsh.
The League of Open Water argues over citizenship and property.
Its members seek civic standing apart from tribe or Hist.
The League has its hall in Gideon.
The Lighter Flotilla is four working hulls moored as houses.
The hulls lie along one timber pier off Lilmoth's east bank.
Market rafts lie on the far side of the pier.
Long-Water Hold is the village of a settled Naga tribe.
The hold stands on the main poling route of the inner swamp.
The hold's people quarrel with their tribeless kin.
A lukiul is an assimilated Argonian who took on Imperial ways.
The Marsh Charter is a tradition of fighters for hire.
The Empire's Fighters Guild charter ended with Imperial rule in Black Marsh.
The Marsh Charter opposes accepting a foreign charter again.
Morrowind is the Dunmer province north of the marsh.
Argonian armies sacked Mournhold in the Fourth Era.
The border between the provinces is cold and resented on both sides.
The Morrowind veterans are Dunmer soldiers of the Accession War.
The veterans did not go home.
The Accession War was fought in the first years of the Fourth Era.
Murkmire is the southern region of Black Marsh, on Oliis Bay.
Murkmire has at least a dozen tribes and no central ruler.
The Naga-Kur rule the inner swamps of Murkmire.
The Murkwater are a Murkmire tribe of hunters and trainers.
Murkwater is also the name of the tribe's village.
Naga are seven or eight feet tall with needle fangs.
The Naga live in the deep parts of the marsh.
Not every Naga is a brigand.
The Naga-Kur are the Naga people who rule the inner swamps.
The Naga-Kur wear the bones of their fallen on their arms.
Neighbouring villages fear the Naga-Kur.
A naheesh is an elder of an Argonian tribe.
The naheesh carries the tribe's sacred croaks and naming secrets.
A naheesh is respected but has no power to rule.
The Night-Reed Chapter is the thieves' guild.
The Night-Reed Chapter is a native guild that works canals, boats and flooded districts.
A new member of the Night-Reed Chapter starts as a lookout.
Nine Bends is built round a Hist, nine bends of river above the port.
The water at Nine Bends is still fresh.
More of the village's adults are away on the downriver roll each year.
The Turning Path runs the temple called the Teeth of Sithis.
The Turning Path teaches change, endings and mourning.
The Turning Path settles quarrels between villagers.
Imperial surveyors abandoned the North Cut after four kilometres.
The villagers quarry the North Cut's stone for their yards.
The North Cut drains water onto two fields and a hamlet.
The Onkobra runs east past Gideon into the interior.
The road beside the Onkobra is muddy.
Red Onkobra clay is a known product of the marsh.
The Padomaic is the ocean on the eastern coast.
The Hist's larger land sank into the Padomaic in the Dawn Era.
Archon faces the Padomaic.
Riverwalk is a halt in a sheltered sea cove.
Root Talk is the convocation of tree-minders and naheesh.
Root Talk governs Helstrom by consensus.
Root Talk is also the name of the sacred croaks.
The Root-Whisper's Hist withdrew after a plague.
The Root-Whisper's tree lies asleep and does not speak.
The Cyrodilic Collections helped the Root-Whisper tribe rise again.
The Waykeepers look after the rootworm routes and their air pockets.
The Waykeepers' routes are secret.
A rootworm station stands at Helstrom.
The Salt-Teeth are pirates who sail inside the Compact.
A boat with the Compact's name may be a raider's.
The Sealed Vault is a stone undercroft beneath a ruined works.
The door of the Sealed Vault was nailed shut two hundred years ago.
The sealing party's note is still nailed to the door and names the contents.
Shadowfen is the north-western region around Stormhold.
Shadowfen borders Morrowind and Cyrodiil.
Shadowfen has ruined temples and Hist trees along its channels.
A Shadowscale is an Argonian born under the sign of the Shadow.
A Shadowscale may not kill another Shadowscale.
Few Shadowscales remain.
Soulrest was the Imperial capital of Black Marsh in the Third Era.
Soulrest lies on the south-west coast by Topal Bay.
Soulrest is contested today.
The Southern Sea lies south of the marsh.
Lilmoth and Soulrest are the province's only cities on the Southern Sea.
Oliis Bay and Topal Bay are parts of the Southern Sea.
The Sul-Xan are a Naga cult that takes souls.
The Sul-Xan wear jade death masks and sacrifice outsiders and Argonians.
Every tribe fears the Sul-Xan.
The Sunken Archive is an order of scholars who argue over who owns knowledge.
Argonians learn magic as a folk skill and have no guild.
The Archive works between local custodians and the foreign mages.
The Synod and the College grew from the Mages Guild.
The Synod forbids necromancy.
The Synod has no hall in Argonia but hunts artefacts through buyers.
Tear is a Dunmer border town on the coastal plain.
The Tear road reaches Tear from Thorn.
House Dres ran its slave trade from Tear.
The Empty Cradle is the order of the Shadowscales.
The masters who gave the Empty Cradle its orders are gone.
Three buyers now bid for the Empty Cradle's work.
The Accord argues over title to the saltrice fields.
The Accord also argues over what the border remembers.
The Accord has a magistracy, a militia hall and a counting floor.
Umbriel is a flying city.
Umbriel destroyed Lilmoth in 4E 48.
Umbriel killed much of the south of Black Marsh.
The Society argues over how 4E 48 should be remembered.
The Society has its archive in Lilmoth.
Some of its people want a memorial place that is not disturbed.
The Unbound Root puts the Hist above every law.
Some of the Unbound Root are victims of state abuse and some are fanatics.
The Unbound Root says real change needs a way to sever the bond.
A cutting is a piece taken from a Hist and planted away from the tree.
The Unbound Root takes cuttings from a Hist.
A xanmeer is a stepped stone pyramid built by the old Argonians.
Most xanmeers are ruins.
The insides of a xanmeer are mazes of traps and relics.
The Xit-Xaht's Hist directs the tribe.
The other tribes fear the Xit-Xaht.
The Xit-Xaht still build in stone.
The Slow Heron is the raft of the boat crew at the Riverwalk stage.
A body was lifted out of the spring water.
Two households at the spring would rather the body was not spoken of.
The tribe charges nothing for the spring water.
Beds and rope at Greenspring cost a great deal.
Two convocation delegations lodge at Greenspring instead of paying the pitch rent at Nine-Trunks.
The delegations want the use of the spring written down before the next convocation.
Nine-Trunks rents convocation pitch at a high rate.
The city spring at Helstrom runs sour on a cycle, and the assembly will not time the cycle in open session.
The Greenspring Hist has begun to sicken.
Four villages send offerings to the shrine each wet season, in rotation.
The offerings now are tools and salt, not symbols.
This year the flooding got worse.
The offerings on the shelf are slowly corroding.
A visitor to Greenspring tastes the water of the pool under the Hist before speaking.
The village's fish traps stand where the free port's boats now load.
The village's claim to the traps and the port's claim to the landing are both old enough to be argued.
The same cut mark shows at the waterline on each of the nine bends.
Nine Bends stopped counting the marks a generation ago.
One of the cut marks is at the village landing.
The refuge downriver has a clutch to name and no Hist of its own.
Nine Bends has offered to do the refuge's naming.
A naming needs the Hist and its hatchery pool.
The camp where the refuge keeps its clutch is a day downriver of the tree.
No keeper at Chasepoint has been paid in two centuries.
A salvage lot at Chasepoint comes off a ship whose owners do not know it sank.
Chasepoint stands on the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland.
A locked chest beside the old stable holds salvage held back from the count.
The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
The Lilmoth council wants lightering licensed.
A hidden cache on the flotilla holds cargo off a hull that never reached the quay.
Riverwalk's people earn their living from the ferry stage and the toll on boats entering the pilgrim water.
Paying the toll to Thorn or to Hissmir counts as taking that side.
The toll is argued over every night.
The villagers sound the way across the cove to the ferry stage every morning.
Boats would pass Riverwalk by if the cove silted up.
At least one faction claims to have found the temple's lost first purpose.
The Clutch accept that the temple's first purpose is lost, and they teach the loss to pilgrims.
The column's men take a levy from the road below the camp.
The toll company's officers want to use the column themselves, not see it cleared.
Gideon's governor will not pay to clear the column.
The column's men stand watches and call the watch on the hour.
The column would disband if Gideon offered a pardon and a wage.
The men of the North Cut Camp take payment each season to keep the track quiet.
Long-Water Hold has begun paying the camp not to work its stretch of the track.
The camp's men cut a tally-stick as a receipt for each payment.
The diggers have left the deep end of the seep.
The seep is being worked out, and each season's cakes lie further from the path.
A giant leech has its den out past the deep end of the seep.
A bone-tag came back to the Tag House from the villages for a woman of the Rose.
Her family were told she walked out of the Rose years ago.
A trafficker moves living people out of the Rose on the papers of the dead.
Tag 17 in the charge book was released after a week with no name given.
Some bone-tags on the Tag House wall are hung for people who are still alive.
The names on the living tags belong to families in Vaunting.
White Rose Prison holds the graves of Argonians who died mid-Owing, far from their Hist.
A diver came up dead on lot four. She had no right to work that lot.
A lot has outlived its last heir. Four families dive it to stake a claim.
Whoever claims a heirless lot pays a share of its worth to the heirs' line.
A drowned diver's basket lies on the deep lot by the fourth lot, eight metres down.
The lost ship's owners keep a counting house in Soulrest, west along the coast road.
The causeway survey left Soulrest east along the coast road, toward the Tag House on the Prison road.
The second family keeps the Fourth Stage. It claims Chasepoint's arrears on the strength of an old Legion posting.
The wreck on the bar carried bonded labourers below deck, so the families will not work it.
Wreckers on the bar hold anyone they pull from the water as crew until the rescue is worked off.
